data.text: Physics support is a required key support in a virtual world generator to make the virtual world behave like the real world. Object motion should be governed by basic laws of mechanics, while collision support requires both detection and response. Physics support should also replicate phenomena such as how light, sound, and smell propagate.
points: Physics support is a required key support in a virtual world generator.
The purpose of physics support is to make the virtual world behave like the real world.
Object motion should be governed by basic laws of mechanics, while support for advanced laws can make motion more realistic.
Collision support should include both collision detection and collision response.
Physics support should also replicate phenomena like how light, sound, and smell propagate.

data.text: Networked collaborative VR is a shared virtual world maintained by a system or server. Users have distinct matched zones that are usually disjoint and distributed globally. The system must manage user interactions and collisions regardless of distance, and the virtual world generator should support eye movements, facial expressions, and body language for social interaction.
points: Networked collaborative VR is a shared virtual world maintained by a system or server.
Users have distinct matched zones that are usually disjoint and distributed globally.
The system must manage user interactions and collisions regardless of distance.
The virtual world generator should support eye movements, facial expressions, and body language for social interaction.

data.text: Developers can build VR experiences from scratch using an SDK or use a ready-made virtual world generator (VWG). While building from an SDK provides maximum control and performance optimization, it requires building physics and audio from scratch and imposes a difficult implementation burden. In contrast, ready-made VWGs allow for faster creation because they include built-in supports, though they may restrict the development of highly original experiences.
points: Developers can build VR experiences from scratch using an SDK or use a ready-made virtual world generator (VWG).
Building from an SDK provides maximum control and performance optimization, but requires building physics, collision, and audio from scratch.
Building from an SDK imposes a difficult implementation burden and requires a lot of effort.
Ready-made VWGs make it easy to create experiences in little time because they include built-in supports.
Ready-made VWGs can restrict highly original experiences because the developer must use the engine's existing functions and algorithms.

data.text: A game engine is middleware that abstracts hardware functionalities, providing a software development environment to build XR experiences. The engine is comprised of several components, such as rendering, physics, and audio engines. Developers use authoring tools to access these functionalities and configure application logic through scripting.
points: A game engine is middleware that abstracts hardware functionalities for XR applications.
It is a software development environment where applications are built on top of the engine.
Game engines comprise various components such as rendering, physics, audio, and networking support.
Authoring tools allow developers to access these functionalities and configure logic through scripting.

data.text: Rendering engines generate 3D graphics using methods like rasterization or ray tracing by using APIs to provide software abstractions of the GPU. Audio engines manage sound generation and processing using a CPU or ASIC, while physics engines simulate physical forces and collisions. These components are often found in game engines, where Unity 3D and Unreal Engine are the market leaders with different licensing and market shares.
points: Rendering engines generate 3D graphics using methods such as rasterization or ray tracing.
A rendering engine is typically built on APIs which provide software abstractions of the GPU.
Audio engines manage sound generation and processing using a CPU or ASIC rather than a GPU.
Physics engines simulate physical forces and collisions within the application.
Unity 3D and Unreal Engine are the most popular game engines, with different licensing and market shares.

data.text: VR applications can be deployed natively using software development kits (SDKs) or over the web. A platform is the combination of hardware and an operating system, while SDKs provide the tools needed to build experiences for those platforms. Native SDKs are categorized by application type and availability, and different head-mounted displays use different VR software development kits.
points: VR applications can be deployed natively or over the web.
A platform is the combination of hardware and an operating system.
SDKs provide the tools to build VR experiences for specific platforms.
Native SDKs are categorized by application type and availability.
Different head-mounted displays use different VR software development kits.

data.text: Web deployment tools can be broadly categorized as cloud hosting and rendering, development support libraries, complete development and deployment tools, generic development editors, and SDK support. Cloud hosting and rendering support tools only provide hosting and rendering over a network. Development support libraries include WebXR, which uses WebGL, and Three.js, which makes WebGL easier for rendering. There are also complete development and deployment tools for applications on the web.
points: Web deployment tools can be broadly categorized as cloud hosting and rendering, development support libraries, complete development and deployment tools, generic development editors, and SDK support.
Cloud hosting and rendering support tools only provide hosting and rendering over a network.
Development support libraries include WebXR, which uses WebGL, and Three.js, which makes WebGL easier for rendering.
Complete development and deployment tools are available for applications on the web.
